overview.description: Bid Whist is a classic American partnership trick-taking game that evolved from standard Whist. It features a competitive bidding auction where partnerships bid for the right to choose the trump suit and determine whether the ranking will be 'Uptown' (High cards win), 'Downtown' (Low cards win), or 'No Trump'. It is particularly celebrated in African-American culture, where it is played with immense skill, sophisticated signaling, and high social energy.

history.origins: Originating in the United States in the late 19th or early 20th century, Bid Whist grew out of the standard Whist brought by European settlers but was heavily adapted by African-American communities into a complex tactical game.
timeline: 1800s: Standard Whist is the dominant trick-taking game.
Early 1900s: Auction-style bidding elements are added, creating Bid Whist.
1940s-1960s: Becomes a foundational social game in African-American neighborhoods and social clubs.
Present: Remains highly popular, with national tournaments and a deep cultural legacy.
history.evolution: The introduction of the 'Kitty' (widow) and the 'Downtown' ranking system were key innovations that added strategic layers unknown in traditional Whist.
history.cultural: Regarded as a game of 'smack talk' and mental dominance. Mastery of Bid Whist is often considered a rite of passage in many communities.

setup.deck: 54 cards: Standard 52-card pack plus two distinct Jokers (Big Joker and Little Joker).
setup.equipment: Standard pack with jokers, score pad.
setup.dealing: Deal 12 cards to each player. 6 cards are dealt face down to the center to form the 'Kitty'.

rules.objective: First partnership to reach a set score (typically 7 or 21) by fulfilling trick-taking contracts.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Auction**: Players bid a number of 'books' (tricks over 6) from 3 to 7, plus a direction (Uptown, Downtown, or No Trump). 2. **Kitty**: High bidder takes the 6-card Kitty into their hand and discards 6 cards. 3. **Trump**: High bidder names the trump suit. 4. **Tricks**: 12 tricks are played. Must follow suit. 5. **Direction**: Uptown (A high), Downtown (A low), No Trump (No trump suit). 6. **Jokers**: Big Joker is the highest card in the game, followed by Little Joker.
keyRules: A bid of '4 Uptown' means the team must win 10 tricks (6+4) with high cards ranking best.
In Downtown, Aces are low and 2s are high.
Failing a contract (getting 'set') results in losing points equal to the bid.

strategy.basic: Don't bid unless you have at least one Joker or two Aces. The Kitty is a gambleâ€”you hope it contains cards that 'fill' your suits.
strategy.intermediate: Counting the Kitty: The high bidder knows 18 cards (12 dealt + 6 kitty). They must use this information to deduce the location of the remaining Jokers and Aces.
strategy.advanced: Signaling: Through the suit led and the timing of high card plays, partners signal their voids and their 'stops' in side suits. Mastering the lead is essential for 'setting' the opponents.
tips: In No Trump, the Jokers are still powerful! Use them to take control of an opponent's long suit.
If you have a 'run' of cards in Downtown (e.g., 2-3-4), you are nearly unstoppable.

list.name: Fixed Kitty
list.description: Kitty size is fixed at 4 cards instead of 6.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variation notes a smaller kitty but engine-level overrides have not yet been specified.

difficulty.easy: Bids based only on card count. Doesn't understand Downtown ranking. Plays high cards blindly.
difficulty.medium: Understands Uptown/Downtown. Bids conservatively. Tracks the Big Joker.
difficulty.hard: Expert signaling. Calculates probability of kitty contents. Perfectly tracks all 54 cards. Aggressively attempts to set opponents on their own bids.

considerations: Must implement two distinct ranking hierarchies (High-Ace vs Low-Ace).
Kitty exchange logic is a complex optimization problem.

additional: Encyclopedia of African American History (Card Games entry)

ante.reason: Bid Whist is a point-based partnership game and does not utilize a monetary or chip-based ante.

deal.reason: The distribution of twelve cards per player and the six-card kitty is handled automatically by the system dealer.

reveal_market.reason: There is no public market in Bid Whist; the kitty is only revealed to the winning bidder.

buy_market.reason: Players cannot purchase cards from any external area; they must succeed using their dealt hand and the kitty.

buy_stock.reason: There is no stock pile to draw from during play; the entire deck is distributed at the start of the round.

fold.reason: All players are committed to participating in every trick of the hand to determine the final point tally.

check.reason: The game uses a trick-taking and bidding structure rather than a vying structure with checks.

call.reason: There is no bet to match in this game; competition is based on bidding trick counts and winning tricks.

bet.reason: Success is measured by total points accumulated on a scorecard rather than through financial betting.

raise.reason: The value of the deal is fixed by the bid and cannot be raised through further wagering rounds.

declare.description: Declare the trump suit and ranking direction.
declare.constraints: Only available to the highest bidder.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands stay private until individual cards are played into tricks; no full-hand reveal phase occurs.

award_pot.reason: Winning points are added to a cumulative partnership total rather than distributed from a physical pot.

play_card.description: Play a card to the current trick; follow suit if possible.
play_card.constraints: Must follow suit; highest card of led suit or highest trump wins.

draw.reason: All cards are distributed at the start; no drawing phase exists during the play of the twelve tricks.

discard.description: Discard six cards to return the hand size to twelve.
discard.constraints: Only available to the winning bidder after taking the kitty.

pass.description: Decline to bid during the auction phase.
pass.constraints: Allowed during bidding when choosing not to increase the contract.

bid.description: Bid a number of books and a direction (Uptown/Downtown).
bid.constraints: Must be higher than the current high bid.

meld.reason: Bid Whist is strictly a trick-taking game and does not involve the formation of sequences or melds.

go_out.reason: The hand terminates automatically once all twelve tricks have been played by all participants.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: All cards are distributed via the deal and kitty exchange; no draw pile exists during trick play.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Jokers are permanent trumps but do not trigger automated secondary engine effects.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: Bidding is performed verbally around the table; no hidden tokens are required.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Bid Whist is a trick-taking game and does not use a capture-from-tableau fishing mechanic.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: The goal is to win a specific number of tricks rather than being the first to empty the hand.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Highest card of led suit or highest trump wins.

customActions.description: Distribute twelve cards to each player and six cards to the kitty.
Place a bid for books (tricks over 6) and direction (Uptown/Downtown/No Trump).
Winning bidder adds the six cards in the kitty to their hand.
Winning bidder discards six cards from hand after taking the kitty.
customActions.constraints: After taking kitty; must reduce hand to 12.

customActions.description: Calculate points awarded or subtracted based on contract fulfillment.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; card rank determines trick wins (varies by Uptown/Downtown).
engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck plus two jokers (often one red and one black). Four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), thirteen ranks each. The jokers are permanent trumps and are the two highest cards; used for Bid Whist where players bid on tricks and direction (uptown or downtown).
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs) plus two jokers. The jokers are always trumps and outrank all other cards. Trump suit is determined by the bid; follow suit when able. In no-trump bids, the jokers may still be the highest cards.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit plus two jokers. In uptown (high) the jokers are highest, then ace down to two. In downtown (low) the jokers are highest, then two up to ace. The bid determines which direction applies for the hand.
engine.dealPattern: Cards are dealt individually to players and the kitty.

hero.title: BID WHIST
hero.subtitle: The Soul of American Whist
hero.tagline: Bid the books. Choose the direction. Command the table.

synthesis.shortDescription: The high-energy evolution of Whist where the players define the rules of engagement. From the high-stakes 'Uptown' power plays to the clever 'Downtown' low-card maneuvers, Bid Whist is a masterclass in partnership strategy and social intuition.

prompts.human: You have the Big Joker and two Aces. The current bid is '3 Uptown'. With your hand and the potential Kitty, can you take 10 tricks? Raise the stakes to '4 Uptown' and call your partner's best suit!
prompts.ai: Game: Bid Whist. Type: Auction Trick-taking. Rules: 54 cards (incl. 2 Jokers). Bid = books over 6 (e.g. 4 = 10 tricks). Direction determines ranking (Uptown A-high, Downtown A-low).

scoring.description: Points are awarded for making the bid (bid amount) or subtracted for getting set.
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to reach 7 or 21 points.

penalties.Getting Set: If the team fails to meet their bid, the bid amount is subtracted from their total score.

scoring.splitRules: Ties are broken by which team won the final hand's auction.

nullReasons.cardValues: Cards contribute to trick wins rather than having discrete point values.
